takeaways: Net bookings fell 18% to $1.60 billion from $1.96 billion a year ago, under the company's own $1.62-1.67 billion guidance (Zacks).
GAAP net loss narrowed to $54.0 million ($0.29 a share) from $133.9 million ($0.73) a year ago.
Recurrent consumer spending, such as in-game purchases, fell 9% in bookings and made up 81% of the total.
GamesBeat reports NBA 2K27 had its second-best bookings launch ever but came in below Take-Two's forecast.

Full-year net bookings guidance stayed at $8.0-8.2 billion, and Q3 guidance is $3.35-3.50 billion. Grand Theft Auto VI launches Nov 19, and CEO Strauss Zelnick said pre-orders continue to reach unprecedented levels.
verdict: Take-Two's quarter was basically the opening act: bookings dipped, the loss shrank, and everyone looked past it to November 19. The company kept its full-year target, which is the sentence the market was waiting for. The whole stock is now one video game's launch week.
